newsitem.title: USA: Dollar posts 32-month high above 112 yen.
newsitem.headline: Dollar posts 32-month high above 112 yen.

text.p: The dollar surged to its highest level in 32 months against the Japanese yen in early trading Wednesday, rising above 112 yen.

The dollar buying was fuelled by a statement made by Japanese Finance Minister Wataru Kubo, who jolted a quiet market when he retracted comments he made in New York on Monday. His remarks Monday had been interpreted by foreign exchange dealers as bad for the dollar.
The dollar peaked at 112.10 yen, its highest level since Jan. 24, 1994, vs. 111.43 at Tuesday's close, but quickly sank back below 112 yen in morning trade.

Kubo on Monday had said the Group of Seven nations meeting in Washington last weekend had welcomed the recent performance of the dollar. He said the group sought a strong dollar, but stopped short of calling for further dollar gains.
But in Tokyo on Wednesday, Kubo denied speaking about future foreign exchange rates.
The dollar, which had sold off initially on Kubo's Monday remarks, pushed higher on the apparent retraction.
"It (the dollar) seems to be breaking out on Kubo coming out with a retractment saying what he said the other day was taken out of context," said James Kemp, chief spot dealer at Citibank.
While dealers did not expect the dollar to retest 112 yen in Wednesday's U.S. session, they said the overall outlook for the dollar remained bullish.
"I'm tempted to say that was the high for today, but long-term support remains strong," said David Ogg, head of foreign exchange trade at HSBC Midland Bank.
The dollar also posted session highs against the German mark just after midday, breaking through the 1.53 barrier to its highest level since July 8.
